posts.title: This geneticist’s age-reversal tech could help restore sight
posts.summary: Yuancheng (Ryan) Lu is obsessed with aging. And with eyes. As he steps outside the Whitehead Institute in Cambridge, Massachusetts, his aviator glasses darken automatically in the sun. Age-related blindness runs in his family. A great-aunt in China, the story goes, was killed crossing a road because she couldn’t see oncoming traffic. And Lu’s own…
bullets: Geneticist Yuancheng Lu has transitioned his academic research on cellular reprogramming into human clinical trials for age-related vision loss.
The therapy, known as ER-100 and developed by Life Biosciences, uses gene therapy to restore damaged optic nerve cells to a youthful state, a process previously validated in mouse models.
The first human injection for glaucoma treatment marks a major milestone in rejuvenation science, moving from theoretical 'fountain of youth' concepts to clinical application.
This development represents a significant shift in biotech, as it targets the underlying biological aging process rather than merely managing symptoms of degenerative eye diseases.

posts.title: This founder is teaching chips how to recycle (their energy)
posts.summary: Throughout the history of the computer chip, engineers have treated waste heat as an inevitable cost of a calculation. Hannah Earley, however, thinks it’s a design choice. Earley, 31, is cofounder and chief technology officer of Vaire Computing, a startup building chips that recycle energy usually thrown away as heat—a strategy known as reversible computing.…
bullets: Vaire Computing is developing 'reversible computing' hardware designed to recycle energy typically lost as waste heat during standard chip calculations.
The startup has successfully demonstrated a patent-pending resonator component that recovers more energy than it consumes, marking a significant proof-of-concept for a 50-year-old theoretical field.
By retaining information rather than erasing it during intermediate computational steps, the technology aims to drastically improve energy efficiency for data centers and consumer electronics.
While the technology remains in early stages, successful commercialization could fundamentally alter the power consumption profile of high-performance computing.

posts.title: This AI entrepreneur is developing agents that can plan ahead for the unexpected
posts.summary: Danijar Hafner’s office in San Francisco’s SoMa district sits mostly empty. His brand-new startup is still in stealth mode and doesn’t even have its name on the door. On the day I visit, there’s only one other person there, and little in the way of furniture. But what it lacks in decor, it makes up…
bullets: Danijar Hafner’s stealth startup is utilizing model-based reinforcement learning to create AI agents capable of navigating unfamiliar physical environments without extensive real-world training.
The approach involves training agents within 'world models'—simulations that emulate physical reality—allowing robots to 'imagine' future outcomes and plan for unexpected scenarios.
This methodology aims to overcome the traditional reliance on massive, iterative real-world trial-and-error, which has historically been a bottleneck for robotics deployment.
The technology is being integrated into humanoid robots, targeting applications where machines must operate autonomously in dynamic, non-standardized human spaces.

posts.title: Xiaomi delivers 30,153 cars in August, down 17.15% year-on-year
posts.summary:
Xiaomi Auto's deliveries rose 9.65% in the first 8 months, reaching 44.8% of its 550,000-unit annual target.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Xiaomi Auto delivered 30,153 vehicles in August, marking a 17.15% year-on-year decline and the second consecutive month of sequential delivery decreases.
With only 44.8% of its 550,000-unit annual target met through August, Xiaomi must achieve a significant ramp-up to an average of 75,881 monthly deliveries for the remainder of the year.
The company has entered the extended-range electric vehicle (EREV) market with the new Sky Nomad series, which saw over 10,000 locked-in orders within four minutes of launch.
Xiaomi faces a challenging market environment as EREV retail sales in China have declined 15.85% year-on-year during the first eight months of 2026.

posts.title: BMW's Neue Klasse iX3 electric SUV appears in China filing ahead of November deliveries
posts.summary:
Pre-orders are open for the China-specific long-wheelbase Neue Klasse iX3, with prices starting at 269,900 yuan ($39,810).
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: BMW has filed the China-specific long-wheelbase Neue Klasse iX3 with regulators, confirming a 235 kW motor and CATL-supplied lithium iron phosphate batteries.
The vehicle features a 3,005 mm wheelbase, which is 108 mm longer than the standard version to accommodate Chinese market preferences for increased rear-seat space.
Pre-orders are currently open with a starting price of 269,900 yuan, and the model is scheduled to begin customer deliveries in November.
The iX3 will integrate advanced technology, including an end-to-end driver assistance system developed with Momenta and an infotainment suite supporting Huawei HiCar and Alibaba's AI.
